items.title: Louis Cottrell, Jr. Interview, 1961-08-25
items.q: Ridgely and, uh, Solid Stanley kept that name going.

ctx.x: You met him? Oh yeah. Is he still living? Oh no. No, he's dead now.

Well it was Willie Bontag. I can remember that picture just as well in Ridgely's home as if I'm looking at it right now. And you say that's where the name, the Tuxedo. That's where it originated, from the club. And Ridgely and, uh, Solid Stanley kept that name going. It was originally Tuxedo

band until they had this. Well by the way, um, speaking of Willie Bontag, I can't pronounce those French names, but Zutty, I used to know him quite well in New York. That's his nephew. And he used to tell me about his uncle, and so when I ran across him on the parade, I recognized the name as soon as I was introduced to the course. Didn't get to talk to him in a half a minute, of course. In those days I didn't, wasn't studying the history as much as I am now. Yeah, nah, yeah. But I was thinking about Zutty. Did…
